title: Harmonize networking TF stack and upgrade AWS provider
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Over time we accumulated multiple near-duplicate networking Terraform modules across infra repos (clusters, shared-services, dedicated-capacity). Each copy diverged in lifecycle handling for EIPs, subnet tagging, and NAT/route table wiring. We're on aws provider 4.x and a mix of Terraform 1.2/1.3 in CI. Upgrading to aws provider v5 and consolidating networking primitives into a single shared module will reduce drift, enable consistent tagging/lifecycle semantics, and unblock future private/VPC improvements.

Scope: create a new canonical module 'networks/v2' (hosted in infra/modules) that codifies: subnet naming and tags, route table lifecycle, NAT gateway provisioning patterns (with an option for managed NAT vs NAT gatewayless pattern), eip lifecycle handling (avoid replacements on tag-only changes), standardized VPC flow log setup, and optional IPv6 enablement flag. Replace duplicates in repos: infra/clusters, infra/shared-services, infra/dedicated. Upgrade provider to aws v5.x across workspaces and update CI Terraform version constraints to >=1.4.

Why now: Provider v5 fixes several subtle semantics around resource replacement and tag handling that have caused noisy plans and accidental recreation of NAT/EIP resources during trivial changes. Consolidating modules will save ~1-2 engineer-days/week in cross-repo debugging and reduce incident surface during infra changes.

Non-goals: This ticket does not address application-level networking (service mesh) or change existing CIDR allocations. IPv6 will be opt-in and not enabled by default. Full Terragrunt refactor is out of scope (we will add thin wrappers where Terragrunt is used).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical module infra/modules/networks/v2 exists with README, examples, and unit tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform)
All staging workspaces (clusters/shared-services/dedicated) successfully switch to the new module and aws provider v5 with zero net resource replacements in plan except intentional changes
CI TF validate/plan runs green for all updated workspaces and format/lint rules pass
Documented migration steps and rollback playbook in Confluence with a post-migration checklist
No increase in infra cost > 5% attributable to the refactor; any increases must be explicitly justified
migration_plan: Create infra/modules/networks/v2 with modular inputs and outputs; include example usage for clusters/shared-services/dedicated
Add provider v5 constraint and bump TF runtime in a dedicated branch; run provider upgrade tool to generate upgrade notes
Smoke-test module locally with a disposable staging VPC (deploy minimal stack) and run terratest integration
Open per-repo migration PRs (infra/clusters, infra/shared-services, infra/dedicated) that switch module source and pin module version
Deploy to staging, run terraform plan and apply under engineering observation window, verify no unexpected replacements
Run downstream e2e tests (console, API) to ensure nothing regresses from networking changes
After 72h of stability in staging, schedule canary rollout to a single low-risk production workspace, monitor CloudWatch/Datadog, then roll forward
Cut release tag infra/modules/networks/v2 and update infra repo docs and onboarding guide
risks: Provider upgrade may change default API behavior leading to resource replacements — mitigated by dedicated smoke tests and careful provider upgrade review
Module API surface change could require material changes in callers — mitigate by providing compatibility inputs and deprecation warnings
Migration timing could collide with unrelated infra changes — coordinate with infra owners via sprint calendar and lock windows
Cost changes if NAT/GW pattern differs — include cost estimate in PR and gate by approval
